before: Every run of an equation claimed its whole font box on the line, so a later, larger run made the line as tall as its font box.
after: The first atom of an equation claims its font box. A later text atom claims its glyph ink, with the math leading of the first atom size above it, and never more than its font box. A later text atom that draws nothing claims no height. Painted equation parts take no pointer input; the equation host does.
reason: Only local equation geometry and line height change. Canonical OMML, offsets, operations, and collaboration data remain unchanged.
